how_to_mine: Follow this plan exactly. Each lens agent reads only its pages (all are in the corpus; read them with `show <source_id> --around TEXT` or `--lines A:B`, tables with `tables <source_id>`), answers its demand items, and records each item as filled (fact ids), contradicted (what the page says instead) or not-found (where you looked).

Write facts in files of 10 to 25 facts: _build/work/29-elasticache/facts-<lens>-NN.json (lens file names: numbers, behavior, faq), then `facts add --file <that file> --by mine-29-<lens>`. Table rows and value lines: prefer `facts adopt` (--table/--row, --sentence, --heading). Every quote is copied verbatim from the page snapshot (.txt), never from full.md (full.md hits are pointers) and never from memory.

Each quote must carry every clause, scope, condition and exception of the claim on its own. When the condition stands in the next sentence (for example 'This capability is not available for Memcached.' or 'Durability is currently supported with node-based ElastiCache.'), include that sentence in the quote; otherwise narrow the claim. Entail votes run on Opus and mark a clause found only in the surrounding text as partial.

Fact service key: `elasticache` for every ElastiCache fact; ids start with it, for example `elasticache-nodes-per-region`. Neighbour facts: DynamoDB Accelerator `dax` (chapter 28), Application Load Balancer sticky sessions `elb` (chapter 14), RDS read replicas `rds` (chapter 26), API Gateway caching `api-gateway` (chapter 33, same wave), Database Savings Plans `savings-plans`, Well-Architected `well-architected`. Add a neighbour fact only after `facts list --service <key>` shows no verified fact that already answers it; reuse the existing id in the demand record when one exists.

Every hard fact (number, limit, default, price, date, can/cannot, only/always/never) carries `question` (the demand question it answers) and at least two displays for kinds behavior, capability, restriction and default (brief gate B12). A display of a number-free fact is a verbatim phrase of at most 8 words from its quote (RULINGS 2026-10-11).

Engine names: write facts with the names the page uses (Valkey, Memcached, Redis OSS). Where a quote says 'Redis OSS' and an older exam would say 'Redis', keep the quote as is; the writer handles 'formerly Redis'.

Scope matters in this guide: many statements hold only for node-based clusters, only for serverless caches, only for cluster mode enabled, or only for one engine. Put that scope in the claim and make sure the quote states it (a table row plus its header, or the heading via `--heading`).

Changes: a fact touched by a change item sets `changed` (date, old value only if a saved page states it verbatim) and `change_items`. A feature GA after 2026-07-15 gets the note `not examinable yet` (public endpoints for ElastiCache Serverless, 2026-09-29). Current truth comes from the guide, quotas and pricing pages; WhatsNew rows and What's New pages give dates and deltas only.
Case-study facts have kind `case-study` and a quote of at most 25 words.

numbers+changes.job: Every number, limit, default and price for ElastiCache: adopt rows from the two quota pages first, then the shard, replica, backup and serverless pages for limits and defaults, then the pricing page for price dimensions, ECPU rules, Valkey discounts, reserved nodes and data tiering, then the SLA. Then one change fact per change item d019 to d026 with the date from the WhatsNew history row (verbatim row) and a pointer to the current-truth fact. Kinds: limit, quota, default, price, change.
watch: Quotas: the guide page (quota-limits) has 'Default value' with no Adjustable column; the General Reference table has 'Adjustable'. Adopt the row from the page that states what the claim needs; do not add both as competing facts.

The quota row 'Nodes per cluster (cluster mode enabled)' and the shard and replica maxima on the Shards page must agree; if they disagree, record the conflict in the demand note and add the quota-page value.

Durability (d023): the durability page says 'now supports' without a date and SelectEngine says 'Valkey 9.0 and later'. Do not invent a GA date; the Valkey 9.0 What's New page (2026-05-05) gives the engine date only. If no page states the durability launch date, mark the date not-found.
The 'Redis' to 'Redis OSS' rename date is listed as missing in FRESHNESS; mark not-found unless a saved page states it verbatim.
Pricing page numbers vary by Region: a price fact names its Region and the page's own example; prefer dimension and percent facts over per-hour prices.

behavior+decisions.job: Can / cannot / only / by default claims and decision facts: caching strategies (lazy loading, write-through, TTL, eviction), access patterns, session store and statelessness, replication groups, cluster modes, Multi-AZ, read replicas, Global Datastore, backups, durability, scaling, network placement, encryption and authentication, data tiering; neighbour comparisons (DAX, RDS read replicas, API Gateway caching, sticky sessions); the facts behind Callvale's decision (d066, d067); two case-study facts (d068, d069). Kinds: behavior, capability, restriction, default, decision, case-study.
watch: SelectEngine is a comparison table whose rows hold version qualifiers ('4.0.10 and later', 'Valkey 9.0 and later'): quote the row with its header so the engine column is clear, and keep the version condition in the claim.
Memcached backup: the table row says 'For serverless caches only, not applicable to node-based clusters'. A claim 'Memcached has no backup' is wrong as a universal; scope it to node-based clusters.

Multi-AZ: automatic failover is 'Optional' for cluster mode disabled and 'Required' for cluster mode enabled (SelectEngine). Check AutoFailover for the default on new clusters before writing a default fact.
Global Datastore promotion: confirm on the FAQ (question 28) whether failover is automatic before writing a can/cannot fact.
www/caching/* and the Builders' Library are AWS pages but marketing or essay text: quote whole sentences and keep hedges ('can', 'often').
Callvale story values (20 queries, 80% of reads, 60 seconds, two Availability Zones) are story data, never facts; ground only the AWS behaviour each reason names.
Case studies: Beat, Floward, The Pokemon Company, SmartNews and Tonkean redirect to the listing page (brief fetch_failures); use only Wakelet, Glossika, Amazon Ads, Talabat.

faq.job: Verbatim FAQ answers for the FAQ quick-fire section (pick the 8 to 10 strongest of d070 to d087) and for the Signals table. Quote whole sentences from the FAQ snapshot. Where an FAQ answer disagrees with the guide, record the guide as current truth and note the FAQ wording in the demand record instead of adding a contradicting fact.
watch: The FAQ list (work file faq-elasticache.txt) has 56 questions in 11 sections; item 56 is an empty 'NA' entry, skip it.
Public endpoints (d081) are not examinable yet (2026-09-29): add the fact with that note.

rules: Quote from page snapshots only; full.md hits are pointers.
A demand item becomes filled, contradicted (with what the page says) or not-found.
Current truth comes from the guide, quotas and pricing pages; What's New pages and history rows give dates and deltas only.
Files of 10 to 25 facts; every quote verbatim and complete for its claim; `--by mine-29-<lens>`.
